newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suicide said possible in Busang geologist's death.
newsitem.headline: Suicide said possible in Busang geologist's death.

text.p: Filipino geologist Michael de Guzman, who fell out of a helicopter on his way to the huge Busang gold property he helped discover in East Kalimantan, was ill and may have committed suicide, officials said on Friday.
Among several letters found in de Guzman's bag, left behind in the Allouette 3 helicopter, was one addressed to his wife saying that he was suffering from acute Hepatitis B.

"There were several letters in the bag, along with some medicine. One letter addressed to his wife said he was suffering from acute Hepatitis B," Sugianto, head of the airport in East Kalimantan capital Samarinda, told Reuters by telephone.
"It looks like it was suicide," he said. "Inspection of the helicopter showed that everything was in good condition."

Search and rescue officials said on Thursday that de Guzman was missing after the back door of the helicopter burst open 17 minutes after taking off from Samarinda airport on Wednesday morning on its way to the Busang property in the Kutai regency.

They said the helicopter had been chartered by Canadian company Bre-X Minerals Ltd, where de Guzman was chief geologist, from PT Indonesia Air Transport and was piloted by Captain Eddy Tursono, who was accompanied by an engineer.
The Busang motherlode, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 80 million ounces of gold currently worth around $25 billion, is the biggest gold find this century.
Bre-X has entered into an an agreement with Indonesian partners and the U.S. mining giant Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop Busang.
Sugianto said the items contained in de Guzman's bag had been handed over to the police. The police officer holding the contents could not be immediately reached for comment.
Sugianto said search and rescue operations resumed early on Friday with the help of local residents and Bre-X employees.
Frank Cimafranca, third secretary and consul at the Philippine Embassy, said there had been no official word from the authorities on the search for de Guzman.
"All we know at the moment is what we have been reading in the newspapers," he told Reuters. "We are quite disappointed there has been no official communication from the authorities."
"At this stage, we cannot discount all possibilities," he said, referring to de Guzman's possible suicide.

He said the embassy would like to take custody of de Guzman's personal belongings and hand them over to his next of kin in the Philippines. "According to our records, he has a wife in Quezon City," he said.
